title: Rewrite request handoff and regional prioritizer to simplify routing hotpaths
creator: Priya Shah
description: Background: The smart routing layer has accumulated multiple ad-hoc handoff paths between the policy evaluator, the regional admission logic, and fallback coordinator. This results in inconsistent decision ordering, extra allocations on the hotpath, and duplicated telemetry that increases p90 latency under surge. Goal: Replace the current multi-stage handoff flow with a single, compact 'handoff-and-prioritizer' component that centralizes region scoring, admission checks, and deterministic fallback selection. The new component should be lock-free on the request hotpath, minimize allocations, and emit a unified trace/span that captures decision rationale for observability and postmortems.
technical_approach: Introduce a HandoffPrioritizer interface with a single Evaluate(requestCtx) -> RankedRegionList signature
Move scoring heuristics (region affinity, capacity headroom, cost tier) into weight functions and make them pluggable for experiments
Replace several mutable maps with a compact arena-backed snapshot used for per-request evaluation to avoid GC churn
Convert synchronous policy gates to pre-compiled predicate tokens so evaluation becomes a few arithmetic ops in the hotpath
Add a light-weight fallback selector that can choose a compatible region-model pair without issuing network calls during evaluation
Add comprehensive unit/bench tests and a microbenchmark harness to measure p50/p95/p99 before/after changes
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p95 routing latency on benchmark harness reduced by >= 20% for 128 concurrent clients
Hotpath allocations reduced by >= 50% as shown by Go pprof allocations/second
No customer-facing behavior change for current canary traffic when running with feature gate off
New unified trace/span emitted for every decision containing region_score, policy_flags, and fallback_reason fields
All new code covered by unit tests and load microbenchmarks; PR has at least two engineering approvals
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Design and proto (1 week): design API, review with infra and platform teams, sketch benchmarks. Doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/hand-off-prioritizer-spec
Phase 2 - Library impl (2 weeks): implement HandoffPrioritizer with weight functions and arena-backed snapshot, add unit tests
Phase 3 - Integration (1 week): wire into router hotpath behind feature gate, add telemetry and unified spans
Phase 4 - Canary and metrics (2 weeks): run canary in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic, compare latency/allocations, iterate
Phase 5 - Rollout and cleanup (1 week): flip feature gate, remove legacy handoff code, update docs and runbook
risks_and_mitigations: Regression in route correctness: mitigate with a staged canary, a strict verification test (deterministic request replay) and alerting on routing divergence
Unseen latency in worst-case scoring: mitigation by adding a fallback fast-path that returns precomputed region ranks when requestCtx indicates common patterns
Telemetry gaps during rollout: mitigation by dual-writing old and new spans for 1 week and running comparison dashboards
Edge cases for custom policy adapters: mitigation by keeping adapter shim layer in place during integration and adding adapter conformance tests
notes: Related incident: surge-2025-11-12 exposed contention in region admission maps; incident timeline: https://drive.redwood.ai/incidents/surge-2025-11-12
Prototype microbench results: local harness shows 28% reduction in p95 for synthetic small-seq workloads (raw results in https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/hand-off-proto-2026-02-28)
Design review scheduled: 2026-02-24 with infra and platform leads
Conservative fallback policy chosen for initial rollout to avoid capacity oversubscription
